fields.asked: Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour). What this is for. The first outside test will be a small team on Jira who already use agents and are looking to have agents build their product. John has used Harbour on Jira for a few weeks: 'it's mostly fine except for the gaps that you've identified.' The gaps: Harbour can't create a Jira issue, so on Jira the loop can't file a task with the person's words sealed, mint a Periodical, or file what a task's last step files; Jira can't yet hold the block that keeps the person's words exactly as asked. What we want. On a Jira-backed workspace, the loop does what it does on Linear: a task can be filed with the person's words sealed, a Periodical can be minted, and a task's last step can file what it files. It's checked on John's own Jira, which is already in real use. Every change names what it retires. Questions: settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.
fields.done-when: On John's Jira a task filed through Harbour keeps the person's words sealed, a Periodical mints, and a task's last step can file.

fields.answer: Shape B: the exact words live in a Jira issue entity property harbour.asAsked = { v: 1, words, rendered }, written in the same create/edit request; the description holds an ordinary block (h2 'As asked', markdownToAdf(words), italic end line). On read, the region still rendering to `rendered` serves the exact words; otherwise the current rendering (Linear parity). descriptionRoundTrip becomes write-then-read, property included, so providerHoldsAsAsked turns true with no change to lib/as-asked-seal.js.
fields.basis: policy: the ask's 'settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls go to him'
fields.why: B is the only shape that is exact for agents and leaves Jira looking like Jira for its people; the first-dispatch seal will touch tickets the team wrote. A (code-block carrier) turns every formatted Jira-native ticket into a grey raw-Markdown box; C (normalised baseline) needs John's ruling and B doesn't; a lossless codec is whack-a-mole. Would change: site refuses properties in bodies (then separate PUT, still B); John wants the ask shown verbatim as code (A); John rules render-exact acceptable (C).

pieces.session-1: Session 1: the seal (lands alone). Witnesses are unit tests against fake-client.js. (1) A pure region module beside the provider reads and writes the block. It imports AS_ASKED_HEADING, AS_ASKED_END, splitAsAsked and sealAsAsked from lib/as-asked.js and never retypes their spellings; adf.js stays import-free. The reader finds the region by nodes: an h2 whose text is the heading's text, then a paragraph whose plain text is the end sentence, regardless of marks, and applies the same position rule splitAsAsked applies. If the region's current rendering equals the stored rendered, it serves the exact words; if not, a human edited it in Jira and it serves what the region renders now, behind canonical markers. Without the end paragraph or the heading there is no block. A property with no region is ignored. Witness: reader tests for kept, edited-in-Jira, edited-below-the-line, end line deleted, end line re-marked (_..._ or plain), localId added, stale property with no block. (2) Comparison is on rendered content, never ADF hashes (Jira adds localId on ordinary saves). (3) Every description read in index.js goes through the one reader. Single-issue reads (fetchIssueFields, context issue, parent, issueDescription) fetch with properties=harbour.asAsked; the bulk path does not (display only, converted words). client.getIssue gains properties and the fake honours it. Witness: a test fails if adfToMarkdown is applied to a description field in index.js outside the reader. (4) updateIssue writes the property in the same PUT whenever the new description holds a block, words from splitAsAsked of what it was handed; no block, no property. client.updateIssue and the fake accept properties. Witness: byte equality of words after filing, a later write of what was read, a description/below write, and a human edit below the line. (5) descriptionRoundTrip becomes write-then-read, property included; providerHoldsAsAsked turns true with no change to lib/as-asked-seal.js apart from its stale header. Witness: Jira cases of as-asked-create-seal, as-asked-dispatch-seal and as-asked-readers flip from skipped to sealed and kept (* a bullets, *em*, a fence with a blank line, trailing spaces). (6) Size guard: Jira limits an entity property value to about 32 KB (builder confirms from Atlassian's docs). Too large: descriptionRoundTrip reports a non-kept read-back, so the lane files unsealed with the existing log line; updateIssue refuses with a 422 naming the size, before any write. Witness: an oversized body is filed unsealed with the log line; an oversized updateIssue writes nothing.
pieces.session-2: Session 2: creation. (7) Client createIssue (POST /rest/api/3/issue, fields and properties) and getCreateMeta; provider createIssue creates, then re-reads and returns the canonical issue; property from splitAsAsked of the description given. createFields() becomes title, description, teamId (a Jira project key); apiWriteFields() adds projectId (an epic: parent on team-managed, Epic Link via _resolveEpicLinkFieldId on company-managed) and parentId, not stateId. (8) Issue type chosen inside the provider from createmeta: prefer Task, else first standard non-subtask at level 0; subtask type with a parent. A required field with no default beyond the basics returns 422 naming it and creates nothing. Cached briefly per site and project. (9) All three lanes work on the Jira fake end to end; inlineCreate turns true through supports('createIssue'); getCreateTaskUrl stays overridden because ui.write derives from it. (10) Retires: the deep-link create path on Jira; inlineCreate: false; the stale LIN-1557 comments; the 'Jira is skipped today' seal claims in lib/as-asked-seal.js, lib/as-asked.js and the descriptionRoundTrip comment; README line 60 and docs/proxy-integration.md 'Jira files unsealed'; CONSEQUENCE_TEST's 'cannot create tickets' branch; 'Linear task' wording in lib/periodicals.js. (11) Prompt-text changes re-measured against prompt-size-budget and the Periodical hash; rebase first.
pieces.session-3: Session 3: live check and leftovers (needs John's Jira credentials). (12) On John's Jira: file one task through Harbour, mint one Periodical, perform one last-step filing; re-read each and check kept; write below the line once and re-check; record the createmeta result and whether the site accepted properties in create and edit bodies. Site rejects properties: separate PUT /issue/{key}/properties/harbour.asAsked straight after, failure through PartialWriteError (still shape B). A required custom field is a finding for a follow-up ticket. No credential: park it as a handoff to John (what to run, what to paste back), not as done. (13) File one ticket for the markdownToAdf fenced-block-with-blank-line bug; create docs/areas/providers.md with two Waiting entries: widening the D1 writer vocabulary, and an explicit 'holds verbatim text' provider capability.

fields.asks: The node rule and the markdown rule disagree about what counts as an end line. hasMarkerLine and splitAsAsked match the end sentence only with its *...* exactly; the planned ADF reader matches a paragraph whose plain text is the end sentence, whatever its marks. Words holding that sentence as plain or _..._ text are sealed, then the node reader closes the region early, the digest misses, and the tail is served as if below the line. Nobody is told. Decide which up front.
options: make hasMarkerLine catch the plain-text form too
have the node rule take the last matching paragraph before non-region content
fields.if-unanswered: Silent misread of the words' tail; the pure descriptionRoundTrip catches it only if it runs the same node reader.

fields.says: A Jira description has one reader and one writer: readDescription and holdAsAsked in lib/providers/jira/as-asked-region.js. They are the only code that knows the ADF region and the harbour.asAsked entity property, and every provider-side getIssue passes AS_ASKED_READ. Shape B keeps the words in two places, safe only while one module knows both. A new description read that calls adfToMarkdown directly serves converted words and breaks the seal without anyone being told; tests/unit/jira-as-asked-region.test.js fails on it.

Decide whether the words are kept by comparing renderings, never ADF. Jira stamps localId and similar attributes on ordinary saves, and adfToMarkdown ignores them. A hash of the ADF would read every human save as an edit.

The region reader accepts an end line whatever its marks, which is looser than splitAsAsked. It stays safe because descriptionRoundTrip runs the same reader the reads do, so a block the reader would misplace is refused at filing. Keep the seal's check and the reads on one reader. (Survey open-0.)
